walkthroughs.body_html: Cloward & Ohlin (1960) argued Merton ignored that illegitimate means also differ by area. Criminal subculture: stable working-class communities where adult crime gives apprenticeship (e.g. East End). Conflict: disorganised areas, no career criminals, status from gang violence. Retreatist: double failures retreat into drugs.

Miller (1958): working-class crime is not a reaction to middle-class values but expression of distinct focal concerns: trouble, toughness, smartness, excitement, fate, autonomy. These produce crime naturally without strain. Critics: too deterministic and unitary.

Matza (1964): most delinquents are not committed subculturalists — they drift between conventional and deviant values. Sykes & Matza (1957): five techniques of neutralisation excuse deviance: denial of responsibility, injury, victim, condemners; appeal to higher loyalties.
